''Global Sensitivity Analysis. The Primer''<ref name="Primer">{{cite book |vauthors=((Saltelli, A.)), ((Ratto, M.)), ((Andres, T. H.)), ((Campolongo, F.)), ((Cariboni, J.)), ((Gatelli, D.)), ((Saisana, M.)), ((Tarantola, S.)) |date=2008 |title=Global sensitivity analysis : the primer |publisher=John Wiley |url=https://doi.org/10.1002/9780470725184 |isbn=0-470-05997-4}}</ref> by [[Andrea Saltelli]] and other practitioners is an introduction to [[sensitivity analysis]] of model output, a discipline that studies how the uncertainty in model input and model assumptions propagates to model output and model-based inference. The volume was published in December 2007 by [[Wiley (publisher)|John Wiley & Sons]]. The same publisher offered a Chinese translation in 2018.<ref name="PrimerChinese">{{cite book | vauthors=((Wu, Q.)), ((Ding, Y.)), ((Yi, M.)), ((Fan, Q.)) | date= 2018 | title=Global sensitivity analysis ( Chinese version) | publisher=Tsinghua University Publisher | url=http://www.tup.tsinghua.edu.cn/booksCenter/book_05945201.html | isbn=978-7-302-48555-1}}</ref>

== Main==
[[Sensitivity analysis]] applies to all forms of quantification and has been mostly used in relation to [[mathematical model]]ling. It is an ingredient of model validation it that it studies how the uncertainty in the input (data, assumptions) affects the output of the model (inferences, decisions).  
The volume appears as the most cited handbook of sensitivity analysis,<ref name = "timeline">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Tarantola, S.)), ((Ferretti, F.)), ((Lo Piano, S.)), ((Kozlova, M.)), ((Lachi, A.)), ((Rosati, R.)), ((Puy, A.)), ((Roy, P.)), ((Vannucci, G.)), ((Kuc-Czarnecka, M.)), ((Saltelli, A.)) | journal=Environmental Modelling and Software | title=An annotated timeline of sensitivity analysis | volume=174 | article-number=105977 | date=1 March 2024 | issn=1364-8152 | doi=10.1016/j.envsoft.2024.105977}}</ref><ref name=GS2008>{{Citation | vauthors=((Google Scholar)) | year=2024 | title=''Global sensitivity analysis: the primer'' (2008)| url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=vqhLsGkAAAAJ&citation_for_view=vqhLsGkAAAAJ:aEW5N-EHWIMC | access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref>  and tackles questions such as ''How sensitive are results to an assumed input value?''; ''What variables are driving conclusions?''; ''Can I simplify this model?''; ''What parameter levels will lead to a desired outcome?''<ref name="Shepherd_BE">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Shepherd, B. E.)) | journal=Biometrics | title=''Global Sensitivity Analysis. The Primer'' by SALTELLI, A., RATTO, M., ANDRES, T., CAMPOLONGO, F., CARIBONI, J., GATELLI, D., SAISANA, M., and TARANTOLA, S. | volume=65 | issue=4 | pages=1311–1312 | date=1 December 2009 | issn=0006-341X | doi=10.1111/j.1541-0420.2009.01343_7.x}}</ref>  Exercises and solutions are provided at the end of each chapter.<ref name="Shepherd_BE"/><ref name="Liu_S" /> A table of content is offered by statistician Shuangzhe Liu in his review of the book:<ref name="Liu_S">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Liu, S.)) | journal=International Statistical Review | title=''Global Sensitivity Analysis: The Primer'' by Andrea Saltelli, Marco Ratto, Terry Andres, Francesca Campolongo, Jessica Cariboni, Debora Gatelli, Michaela Saisana, Stefano Tarantola | volume=76 | issue=3 | pages=452–452 | publisher=International Statistical Institute | date= 2008 | issn=0306-7734}}</ref>

The volume reads as a compilation of the authors' and other practitioners' previous works aimed to a simulation-based sensitivity analysis that is efficient and carefully designed.<ref name="Shepherd_BE" /> Among the authors cited in the book is statistician [[Edward E. Leamer]] who introduced the term ">Global sensitivity analysis".<ref name="Shepherd_BE" />  
The first chapter offers a sort of philosophical introduction to discipline followed by an anticipation of the methods that will be treated in Chapters 3,4,5.<ref name="Shepherd_BE" /> The second chapter treats experimental design, an important topic since simulation work may be computer time intensive and a well-designed experiment are useful. This chapter introduces to several designs including [[Latin hypercube sampling]] and [[Quasi-Monte Carlo method|Quasi random sampling with Low-discrepancy Sequences]],<ref name="Shepherd_BE" /> [[Sobol sequence]] specifically.<ref name="Primer" />{{rp|p=82–89}} 
Chapter 3 deals with the [[Elementary effects method|method of elementary effects]], a derivative based approach that changes the value of a single factor then repeats this at several points in the space of the input, also illustrating how to proceed to treat factors in groups.<ref name="Shepherd_BE" /> The method is due to statistician [[Morris method|Max D. Morris]].<ref name="Chernick_M" />
Chapter 4 deals with the [[variance-based sensitivity analysis|variance-based methods]] that are the authors' recommended best practice.<ref name="Shepherd_BE" /> These permit to compute the first order effect of a factor as a contribution to the variance of the output, its interaction terms, as well as a total effect.<ref name="Shepherd_BE" /> Chapter 5 presents [[Sensitivity analysis#Monte Carlo filtering|Monte Carlo filtering]]  and [[Metamodeling]]. Three worked example are presented in chapter 6 using different methods and discussing when to use what.<ref name="Shepherd_BE" /> An afterword concludes the volume with a discussion of possible mode use and misuse,<ref name="Shepherd_BE" />  and the problems of model validation.<ref name="Chernick_M" /> 
Thus, the volume tackles theory and practice of sensitivity analysis, offering  motivation for the analysis, reviewing required statistical concepts, and providing a guide to potential applications in several chapters, see the examples in chapter 6.<ref name="Liu_S"/>

==Reception==
According to Bryan E. Shepherd<ref name="Shepherd_BE"/> the book is to be praised for clarity of exposition, wealth of examples, and solved exercises, while a limitation is that it appears written more for mathematical modelling and simulation than for statistical modelling, though another reviewer<ref name="Chernick_M">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Chernick, M.)) | journal=Technometrics | title=''Global Sensitivity Analysis, the Primer'' | volume=50 | issue=4 | page=548 | publisher=American Society for Quality | date= November 2008 | issn=0040-1706}}.</ref>  finds the book instructive for statistical models as well. The application of this primer to different kind of models is attested by the tens of thousands of citations in academic articles.<ref name="GS2008"  /><ref name="timeline" /> 
The book is seen<ref name="Liu_S" /> as a "welcome addition to its sister volume" ''Sensitivity Analysis in Practice: A Guide to Assessing Scientific Models'',<ref name="Saltelli_Al_2004">{{cite book | vauthors=((Saltelli, A.)), ((Tarantola, S.)), ((Campolongo, F.)), ((Ratto, M.)) | date= February 2004 | title=''Sensitivity Analysis in Practice'' | publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Ltd | url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1002/0470870958 | doi=10.1002/0470870958 | isbn=0-470-87093-1}}</ref> reviewed in,<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Paruggia, M.)) | journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association | title=''Sensitivity Analysis in Practice: A Guide to Assessing Scientific Models'' | volume=101 | issue=473 | pages=398–399 | date= 2006 | doi=10.1198/jasa.2006.s80}}</ref><ref name="McCulloch">{{cite journal | vauthors=((McCulloch, A.)) | journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A: Statistics in Society | title=''Sensitivity Analysis in Practice: A Guide to Assessing Scientific Models ''| volume=168 | issue=2 | page=466 | date=1 March 2005 | issn=0964-1998 | doi=10.1111/j.1467-985X.2005.358_16.x}}</ref> see citations.<ref name="GS2004">{{Citation | vauthors=((Google Scholar )) | year=2024 | title=Sensitivity analysis in practice: a guide to assessing scientific models (2004)| url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=vqhLsGkAAAAJ&citation_for_view=vqhLsGkAAAAJ:HbR8gkJAVGIC | access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref>
